probe.question: Can BitTorrent Mainline DHT/BEP 5 act as namespace-free passive provider discovery for exact Git commit 573f2f0a00718109e2cd2fc1c1c9bf2f5a0404de merely by using the same 20 bytes as info_hash?

sources.qualification: BitTorrent Enhancement Proposal 5, official Mainline DHT protocol
BitTorrent Enhancement Proposal 3, official v1 protocol/metainfo semantics

observations: BEP 5 get_peers takes an info_hash argument described as the 20-byte infohash of the target torrent and returns peers for that torrent swarm when known.
BEP 3 defines the 20-byte torrent infohash as SHA-1 of the bencoded info value from the torrent metainfo.

Therefore a DHT lookup whose info_hash bytes equal a Git commit SHA-1 is semantically a lookup for a torrent whose info dictionary hashes to those bytes; the protocol does not bind returned peers to the Git commit object that happens to have the same 20-byte digest.
No independently pre-existing torrent/infohash residency for the target bytes was established, and this slice performed no announce_peer, torrent creation, publication, or external mutation.
probe.inference: Reusing the Git commit SHA bytes as a BEP 5 info_hash does not create an exact object-identity bridge from Git commit semantics to BitTorrent torrent semantics. Any provider result would identify peers for a torrent info dictionary, not providers of the Git commit object, unless an independently established mapping existed outside BEP 5.
probe.tested_scope: BEP 5 passive get_peers provider discovery and BEP 3 v1 infohash semantics for the exact 20-byte value 573f2f0a00718109e2cd2fc1c1c9bf2f5a0404de; no network mutation, no torrent publication, no repository namespace, no target residency assumption.
